slots.practicalActivity: In your Trailhead Playground, open the Reports tab and click New Report; browse the report type picker and compare a standard 'Opportunities' type against 'Accounts with Contacts', noting which fields each one exposes before building anything.
slots.deliverable: A written comparison of 2 standard report types, listing which object's fields each one exposes and which relationship (with / with-or-without) governs it.

slots.practicalActivity: Start a new report on the Opportunities report type, name it 'Open Pipeline by Stage', build it using the Outline, Filters, and Preview panels, then Save & Run it.
slots.deliverable: One saved and run report named 'Open Pipeline by Stage' on the Opportunities report type.

slots.practicalActivity: On Open Pipeline by Stage, add a standard filter restricting Stage to open stages, then add one field-to-field filter and one cross filter (for example Accounts without Contacts) to see how each behaves differently from a plain value filter.
slots.deliverable: The Open Pipeline by Stage report updated with a standard filter, a field-to-field filter, and a cross filter, each documented with how it changed the result count.

slots.practicalActivity: Group Open Pipeline by Stage by the Stage field to turn it into a Summary report, then add Close Date grouped by Calendar Month as a nested grouping, and record the resulting subtotals and grand total.
slots.deliverable: A Summary report grouped by Stage and nested by Close Date (Calendar Month), with its subtotals and grand total recorded in writing.

slots.practicalActivity: Convert a copy of the report to Matrix format by dragging Opportunity Owner into Group Rows and Stage into Group Columns, then read the grid to identify which owner has the most pipeline concentrated in a single stage.
slots.deliverable: A Matrix report grouped by Opportunity Owner (rows) and Stage (columns), with a written note naming the owner whose pipeline is most concentrated in one stage.

slots.practicalActivity: Switch a copy of the report to Joined format, add a second block built on a different report type (for example Cases), set Group Across Blocks to a shared field such as Owner, and add one cross-block summary formula comparing a value from each block.
slots.deliverable: A Joined report with 2 blocks grouped across a shared field, plus one working cross-block summary formula.

slots.practicalActivity: On an Opportunities report, add a row-level formula calculating days-to-close (CLOSE_DATE - DATEVALUE(CREATED_DATE)), then add a summary formula calculating win rate (WON:SUM / CLOSED:SUM), validating each before applying it.
slots.deliverable: An Opportunities report containing one validated row-level formula (days-to-close) and one validated summary formula (win rate).

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Bucket Column on Billing Country (or another picklist/text field) named Region, define at least 2 named buckets, leave at least one source value Unbucketed on purpose, then group the report by the new Region bucket column.
slots.deliverable: A report containing one Bucket Column with 2+ named buckets, grouped by that column, with the Unbucketed Values list reviewed in writing.

slots.practicalActivity: Independently build a brand-new report from scratch (not a copy of this chapter's reports) on a different report type, applying filters, grouping into Summary or Matrix format, a row-level or summary formula, and a bucket column, without lesson-by-lesson instructions.
slots.deliverable: One independently built report, on a new report type, using at least 4 of this chapter's tools (filters, grouping, formulas, bucketing).

slots.practicalActivity: Take Open Pipeline by Stage and the Lesson 6 Joined report and write a one-paragraph justification for each: why that specific format (Summary, Matrix, or Joined) was the right choice over the other formats covered this chapter.
slots.deliverable: A written justification document comparing when to use Summary, Matrix, and Joined formats, referencing your own 2 built reports as examples.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup, build a new Custom Report Type with a standard or custom object as primary, add one related object using the 'may or may not have' relationship, edit the layout to expose at least 5 fields, then flip its status to Deployed.
slots.deliverable: One deployed Custom Report Type with a 'may or may not have' relationship and a custom field layout exposing at least 5 fields.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new report folder named Sales Team, share it with a public group or role at Viewer access while keeping yourself at Manager, then create a subfolder inside it and confirm the subfolder inherited that sharing automatically.
slots.deliverable: One shared report folder (Sales Team) with a subfolder that inherited its sharing, both documented with their access levels.

slots.practicalActivity: Subscribe to one of your reports with a weekly schedule, add yourself and one other user or group as recipients, set Run Report As to another person, and add one condition (for example total pipeline below a threshold) so delivery only fires when it's met.
slots.deliverable: One active report subscription with a schedule, a Run Report As setting, and at least one delivery condition configured.

slots.practicalActivity: Export one report as Details Only (.csv) and the same report as a Formatted Report (.xlsx), open both files, and compare what each one preserves (grouping and subtotals versus flat rows).
slots.deliverable: Two exported files from the same report (a Details Only CSV and a Formatted Report XLSX) with a written comparison of what each preserved.

slots.practicalActivity: Take an unfiltered report over a large standard object (such as Case or Opportunity) and compare it against the same report after adding a selective date-range and status filter, and switching Tabular to Summary format.
slots.deliverable: A written before/after comparison of one report's responsiveness after adding a selective filter and switching from Tabular to Summary format.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a complete Report Management package from scratch for a second fictional team: a new custom report type, a dedicated shared folder, a scheduled subscription with a condition, and an exported CSV, built independently without reusing this chapter's examples.
slots.deliverable: A second, independently built report-management package covering a custom report type, shared folder, scheduled subscription, and export.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new dashboard, save it into the Sales Team folder from Lesson 10, add one Chart widget sourced from Open Pipeline by Stage, and confirm the widget updates after you change the underlying report's filter.
slots.deliverable: One new dashboard, saved in a folder, containing at least one widget sourced from a report, with a confirmed live update after editing that report.

slots.practicalActivity: Add at least 3 more widgets to your dashboard, each a different type (Metric, Table, Gauge, or Funnel) and matched deliberately to the question it answers, using 'Use chart settings from report' for at least one of them.
slots.deliverable: A dashboard with 4+ widgets of different types, each type chosen to match its underlying question, with at least one using inherited chart settings.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a dashboard filter (for example on Owner or Type) to your dashboard, test it as a viewer by selecting a value and confirming every widget updates together, then open the dashboard folder's Share dialog and set a Viewer-level audience.
slots.deliverable: A dashboard with one working interactive filter and a folder shared at Viewer access to a chosen audience.

slots.practicalActivity: Move your dashboard into a shared (non-private) folder if it isn't already, set View Dashboard As to The Dashboard Viewer, enable letting viewers change who they view as, and confirm the 'Viewing as [Name] - Change' banner appears.
slots.deliverable: One dynamic dashboard, confirmed by the 'Viewing as [Name] - Change' banner appearing on the live dashboard.

slots.practicalActivity: Run your dashboard through the lesson's 5-point pre-publish checklist: rewrite any vague widget titles into descriptive ones, reorder widgets so the most important number sits above the fold, and remove or merge any widget that fails the 'could this be cut' test.
slots.deliverable: A revised dashboard with descriptive widget titles, a reordered layout leading with the most important number, and a written checklist confirming all 5 best-practice checks.

slots.practicalActivity: Independently build a second complete dashboard for a different fictional audience (for example support leadership instead of sales), including at least 4 widgets, one dashboard filter, a dynamic 'view as' configuration, and an appropriately shared folder, without reusing this chapter's sales dashboard as a template.
slots.deliverable: A second, independently built dashboard (4+ widgets, 1 filter, dynamic running user, shared folder) for a different business audience.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a pipeline-by-stage Summary report filtered to open Opportunities, add Days in Current Stage and filter for deals open more than 45 days in their current stage, then combine both reports into a pipeline dashboard with a funnel widget, a metric widget, and an at-risk table.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline dashboard with a funnel widget (pipeline by stage), a metric widget (total open pipeline), and a table widget listing deals stuck more than 45 days in their current stage.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Cases report grouped by Status with Priority as a second (Matrix) grouping, add a case-age column for still-open cases, then assemble a service dashboard combining a metric widget (open case count), a gauge (average resolution time vs. target), and a table (cases breaching an age threshold).
slots.deliverable: A service-performance dashboard with a metric widget, a gauge widget, and a table widget, each sourced from a Cases report you built.

slots.practicalActivity: Working from the Meridian Outdoor Supply case study, re-create both fixes against your own data: add a stale-pipeline table alongside your pipeline dashboard's total, and rebuild your service report as a Matrix split by Case Type instead of one blended average.
slots.deliverable: Your pipeline dashboard updated with a stale-pipeline (45+ days) table, and your service report rebuilt as a Matrix split by Case Type, mirroring the case study's 2 fixes.

slots.practicalActivity: Follow the lesson's 6-step build exactly: an Opportunities pipeline-by-stage Summary report, a stale-deals report, a Sales Team folder shared at Viewer access, a new Sales Pipeline Overview dashboard with a funnel and table widget, an Owner dashboard filter, and a weekly Monday-morning subscription with the snapshot attached.
slots.deliverable: A complete Sales Pipeline Overview dashboard with 2 source reports, a shared folder, a dashboard filter, and an active weekly subscription, matching every step of the lesson's build checklist.

slots.practicalActivity: Without re-reading the lesson, rebuild the Sales Pipeline Overview dashboard a second time for a different fictional sales team, reusing none of the original folder, reports, or dashboard, then run it against the self-review checklist from Lesson 18.
slots.deliverable: A second, independently rebuilt Sales Pipeline Overview dashboard (separate folder, reports, filter, subscription) that passes the Lesson 18 self-review checklist.

slots.practicalActivity: Review every report and dashboard built across all 4 chapters of this course as one portfolio: confirm folder sharing is correct everywhere, no report sits undocumented, and write a short walkthrough explaining how you'd extend this analytics setup for a new object the business adds next quarter.
slots.deliverable: A final written portfolio summary of all reports and dashboards built in this course, plus a plan for extending the setup to a new object.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can build real Salesforce reporting end to end: custom report types and filtered summary, matrix, and joined reports, organized and distributed through folders, exports, and subscriptions, and assembled into dynamic, well-designed dashboards that answer a specific sales or service leadership question.
